records.question: How many support tickets were opened by customers in the Fintech industry?
records.final_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n
FROM support_tickets t
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.cust_id
WHERE c.industry = 'Fintech';

records.question: What is the total value of won deals for each customer industry? Return industry and total.
records.final_sql:
SELECT c.industry, ROUND(SUM(d.amount), 2) AS total_deal_value
FROM deals d
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = d.acct_id
WHERE d.status = 'won'
GROUP BY c.industry
ORDER BY c.industry;

records.question: Which account manager owns the most customers? Return their name and the count.
records.final_sql:
SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(*) AS n_customers
FROM customers c
JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id = c.account_manager_id
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name
ORDER BY n_customers DESC, e.employee_id ASC
LIMIT 1;

records.question: How many invoices are currently outstanding (unpaid)?
records.final_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM invoices WHERE status = 'unpaid';

records.question: How many deals have been won, and how many lost?
records.final_sql:
SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM deals
WHERE status IN ('won', 'lost')
GROUP BY status
ORDER BY status;

records.question: How many active subscriptions are on each plan tier?
records.final_sql:
SELECT tier, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM subscriptions
WHERE ended_on IS NULL AND status = 'active'
GROUP BY tier
ORDER BY tier;

records.question: For how many customers does the cached plan_tier disagree with their live subscription tier?
records.final_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n
FROM customers c
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE s.ended_on IS NULL
  AND c.plan_tier IS NOT NULL
  AND s.tier IS NOT NULL
  AND c.plan_tier <> s.tier;

records.question: What is the current list price of the Growth plan?
How many invoices are marked paid but have no recorded payment timestamp?
What is the total outstanding (unpaid) invoice amount, in US dollars?
records.final_sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(
  CASE
    WHEN currency_minor = 1 THEN amount / 100
    WHEN currency_minor = 0 THEN amount
    WHEN issued_at < '2025-07-01' THEN amount / 100
    ELSE amount
  END), 2) AS outstanding_usd
FROM invoices
WHERE status = 'unpaid';

records.question: What is the highest single usage value recorded in any event?
How many usage events have a non-numeric event_value?
records.final_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n
FROM usage_events
WHERE event_value IS NOT NULL
  AND event_value NOT REGEXP '^[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$';

records.question: What is the average event value for the feature 'api.query'?
records.final_sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(
  CASE WHEN event_value REGEXP '^[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$'
       THEN CAST(event_value AS DECIMAL(18,4)) END), 4) AS avg_value
FROM usage_events
WHERE feature_key = 'api.query';

records.question: How many distinct companies are in the customer table? Companies appear under more than one record.
records.final_sql:
-- Strip known corporate suffixes BEFORE stripping punctuation, or the
-- suffix's own letters (inc/llc/...) survive and the duplicate never
-- collapses to the same key.
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT
  TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(company_name), ',? *(inc\\.?|incorporated|llc|ltd\\.?)$', ''))
) AS n
FROM customers;

records.question: Which company names appear more than once after normalizing case, punctuation, and common corporate suffixes (Inc/LLC/Ltd/Incorporated)? Return the normalized name and how many records it has.
records.final_sql:
SELECT norm, COUNT(*) AS n FROM (
  SELECT TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(company_name), ',? *(inc\\.?|incorporated|llc|ltd\\.?)$', '')) AS norm
  FROM customers
) t
GROUP BY norm
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY n DESC, norm ASC;

records.question: How many distinct companies have won at least one deal? A company may hold more than one customer record.
Which company (merging duplicate customer records for the same organisation) has filed the most support tickets? Return the normalized company name and the ticket count.
records.final_sql:
SELECT norm, COUNT(*) AS n_tickets FROM (
  SELECT TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(c.company_name), ',? *(inc\\.?|incorporated|llc|ltd\\.?)$', '')) AS norm
  FROM support_tickets t
  JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.cust_id
) x
GROUP BY norm
ORDER BY n_tickets DESC, norm ASC
LIMIT 1;

records.question: Which company (merging duplicate customer records) has the highest total invoiced revenue in US dollars? Return the normalized company name and the total.
records.final_sql:
SELECT norm, ROUND(SUM(usd), 2) AS revenue_usd FROM (
  SELECT
    TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(c.company_name), ',? *(inc\\.?|incorporated|llc|ltd\\.?)$', '')) AS norm,
    CASE
      WHEN i.currency_minor = 1 THEN i.amount / 100
      WHEN i.currency_minor = 0 THEN i.amount
      WHEN i.issued_at < '2025-07-01' THEN i.amount / 100
      ELSE i.amount
    END AS usd
  FROM invoices i
  JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = i.cust_id
  WHERE i.status <> 'void'
) t
GROUP BY norm
ORDER BY revenue_usd DESC
LIMIT 1;

records.question: How many distinct companies currently have at least one active subscription? A company may hold more than one customer record.
How many usage events occurred on 2026-08-15 in UTC?
records.final_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n
FROM usage_events
WHERE (CASE WHEN source = 'batch' THEN event_ts + INTERVAL 4 HOUR ELSE event_ts END)
        >= '2026-08-15 00:00:00'
  AND (CASE WHEN source = 'batch' THEN event_ts + INTERVAL 4 HOUR ELSE event_ts END)
        <  '2026-08-16 00:00:00';

records.question: How many usage events came from the batch source, and therefore need a timezone correction?
records.final_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM usage_events WHERE source = 'batch';

records.question: For each event source, what is the earliest and latest event timestamp after converting everything to UTC?
records.final_sql:
SELECT source,
       MIN(CASE WHEN source = 'batch' THEN event_ts + INTERVAL 4 HOUR ELSE event_ts END) AS min_utc,
       MAX(CASE WHEN source = 'batch' THEN event_ts + INTERVAL 4 HOUR ELSE event_ts END) AS max_utc
FROM usage_events
GROUP BY source
ORDER BY source;

records.question: How many support tickets reference a customer record that no longer exists?
records.final_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n
FROM support_tickets t
LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.cust_id
WHERE t.cust_id IS NOT NULL AND c.customer_id IS NULL;

records.question: What is the total number of support tickets, including any whose customer record is missing?
records.final_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM support_tickets;

records.question: How many churn records use a reason code that is NOT documented in the schema?
records.final_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM churn_log WHERE reason_code > 4;

records.question: How many customers are still churned, i.e. they churned and have not been won back?
records.final_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM churn_log WHERE recovered_on IS NULL;

records.question: What is the total invoiced revenue in US dollars, excluding voided invoices?
records.final_sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(
  CASE
    WHEN currency_minor = 1 THEN amount / 100
    WHEN currency_minor = 0 THEN amount
    WHEN issued_at < '2025-07-01' THEN amount / 100
    ELSE amount
  END), 2) AS revenue_usd
FROM invoices
WHERE status <> 'void';

records.question: How many invoices are missing the currency unit flag?
records.final_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM invoices WHERE currency_minor IS NULL;

records.question: What is the total value of won deals, net of tax?
How many employees are there in total?
records.final_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM employees;

records.question: How many employees have left the company?
records.final_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM employees WHERE left_on IS NOT NULL;

records.question: What is the largest campaign budget?
records.final_sql: SELECT MAX(budget_usd) AS max_budget FROM campaigns;

records.question: Which industries are represented among customers? List them alphabetically.
How many distinct product SKUs exist in the catalog?
records.final_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sku) AS n FROM product_catalog;

records.question: How many support tickets are marked priority P1?
records.final_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM support_tickets WHERE priority = 'P1';
